messages.subject: Restrict loadings/correlations
parts:
Hi Phil,

In a multidimensional model, is it possible to restrict the item loadings and correlations between factors to be positive? If so, could you please provide a brief example.

Best,
Rico

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Restrict loadings/correlations
parts:
Are you fitting and exploratory or confirmatory multidimensional model? The former is much harder to do, but the latter it's possible by setting lower bound constraints on the a parameters via the mirt.model() syntax. 

Phil

parts:
Thank you for the quick response. I am fitting a confirmatory bfactor model and was hoping there is a way to restrict slopes/loadings to be positive (i.e., in the same manner as variance/standard error can be exponentially transformed when estimating a joint distribution model to prevent negative values). Have I misunderstood, or does LBOUND not work for bfactor() function? I have used CONSTRAIN from mirt.model to set slope equal for certain items, can it also be used to limit the possible range of a parameter?

Sorry the question is unclear.

Best,
Rico

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Restrict loadings/correlations
parts:
The LBOUND input does work for bfactor(), though you're right this looks a little confusing given the 'specific' argument specification. What you can do is approach the problem in two steps if you aren't comfortable with mirt's parameterizations just to see what/how the bfactor() organized the model, then use mirt.model() to declare the specifications. Somethign like this:

mod <- bfactor(data, specific=vec)
coef(mod)

model <- "G = 1-32
               LBOUND = (1-32, a1, 0.0), (1-5, a2, 0.0), (6-10, a3, 0.0)'

and so on. HTH. 
Phil
